exercises.title: Sous-Chef
exercises.brief: Write a chef's specials board. Give it a level-one headline, then list each dish.

starter.html:
Ingredients:

  • 🧈 2 sticks unsalted butter
  • 🥣 3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 🥄 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 🧂 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 🍬 1/4 cup sugar
  • 🥚 4 large eggs
  • 🌼 1 tablespoon vanilla extract
  • 🥛 1/4 cup whole milk

Instructions:

  1. Preheat the oven to 350° F.
  2. Butter two cake pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
  3. Butter the parchment and dust the pans with flour.
  4. Whisk 3 cups flour, the baking powder and salt in a bowl until combined.
  5. Beat the butter and the sugar in a large bowl with a mixer until light and fluffy.
  6. Beat in the eggs, vanilla, and flour, slowly, until smooth.
  7. Divide the batter between the prepared pans and put them in the preheated oven.
  8. Bake for 30-35 minutes, until the cakes are lightly golden on top.
  9. Transfer to racks and let cool 10 minutes, then remove the parchment.
  10. Enjoy! 🤌

exercises.brief: An object holds related values under keys. Create an object called `book` with a `title` and an `author`, then log the title.
exercises.solution:
const book = { title: "River Light", author: "J. Ali" };
console.log(book.title);

exercises.title: Remember a value
exercises.brief: localStorage keeps a value for next time. Save the number 42 under the key `score`, read it back and log it. In this sandbox the practice store resets each time you run the example.

exercises.title: Format a price
exercises.brief: Prices read better with thousands separators. Write a function called `formatPrice` that takes a number and returns it with a comma every three digits, then log `formatPrice(1234567)`.
exercises.origin: After the w3schools price formatter demo
